extraction.name: Pointer Sentinel Mixture Models
extraction.description: Introduces the pointer sentinel mixture architecture for neural sequence models, which combines a pointer network with a standard softmax classifier to improve language modeling, especially for rare words. Achieves state-of-the-art perplexity on Penn Treebank and introduces the WikiText corpus.
extraction.creator: Stephen Merity, Caiming Xiong, James Bradbury, Richard Socher
extraction.citeAs: Merity, S., Xiong, C., Bradbury, J., & Socher, R. (2016). Pointer Sentinel Mixture Models. arXiv preprint arXiv:1609.07843.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The WikiText dataset was constructed using text extracted from Wikipedia articles that fit the Good or Featured article criteria. The text was extracted using the Wikipedia API, then normalized and tokenized using the Moses tokenizer. Words with count below 3 were discarded and mapped to <unk> token.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Wikipedia articles (Good and Featured articles) extracted via Wikipedia API.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Specific sections featuring lists were removed. Minor bugs such as sort keys and Edit buttons were removed. Mathematical formulae and LaTeX code were replaced with <formula> tokens.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Normalization and tokenization using Moses tokenizer, augmented to split numbers (e.g., 8,600 -> 8 @,@ 600). Vocabulary constructed by discarding words with count below 3; out-of-vocabulary words mapped to <unk> token.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The Penn Treebank dataset is limited: tokens are lower-cased, stripped of punctuation, and limited to 10k vocabulary, making it unrealistic for real language use. The WikiText dataset aims to address these limitations.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Language modeling (training, validation, testing). The dataset is intended for evaluating long-range dependencies and handling rare words.
